solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Little woman left with one man should be careful

parts.note: Di is a short form of the woman's name Diana
the Roman numeral for one is I
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A warning that a small woman who has gone off with a man ought to watch her step.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is careful and painstaking in their work is described as diligent, a close synonym.

clue.text: It's mad, having one fixed price

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a rate is a fixed charge or price

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that charging a single flat price is crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in the sense of angry, furious: a synonym.

clue.text: Bury jockey, little fellow after a job?

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
to jockey for position is to vie, compete
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Talk of a small rider from the racing town of Bury who is looking for work.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town, and jockey like a rider; both are verbs here. The question mark marks the definition as a description rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate seeking a post is questioned by an employer at a meeting, so is the person interviewed.

clue.text: Backs last runners in race, not the first

parts.note: the last of something is its end

indicators.note: says the opening letter of the runners' name is dropped

parts.note: the runners in a horse race are horses

explanation.surface: A punter backing the horses at the rear of the field, except the leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' drops the H of HORSES, leaving ORSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a proposal or candidate is to support it: a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Film evidently has repeated twists and turns

indicators.note: signals that the letters are wound round into a new order
says the little word has is used twice in the fodder

explanation.surface: A film that clearly keeps twisting its plot over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' doubles HAS, so the fodder is EVIDENTLY plus HAS plus HAS, fifteen letters that 'twists and turns' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a 1938 Hitchcock thriller, so an example of a film.

clue.text: Maybe immigrants demolish province when coming from east

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left

parts.note: to demolish food is to wolf it down
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: Perhaps incomers from the east will wreck a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when coming from east' turns WOLFNI round. NI, Northern Ireland, is known in the UK simply as the Province.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival of people from abroad is one example of a movement into a country, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Relations coming from a match

parts.note: a match here is a marriage, which brings relatives by marriage on the spouse's side

explanation.surface: Family members turning up from a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sports match; the match is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives acquired through a marriage, such as a spouse's parents, are a family-relation term.

clue.text: Suspension of game, held up — fifty will leave

indicators.note: says the fifty is taken away
in a down clue, held up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: golf is a game
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A game is suspended and delayed, and fifty players walk off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns GOLF into FLOG; 'will leave' removes its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is a suspension of tiny water droplets in air, a scientific description.

clue.text: Place of hospitality and love — use phone freely

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: freely means the letters of the two words are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A welcoming home full of affection where guests may use the phone as they like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges USE PHONE into PENHOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A home where visitors are welcomed at any time is a welcoming venue, an idiom.

clue.text: Like some wickets made somehow to keep dry

indicators.note: the reworked letters hold the dry abbreviation inside
somehow says the letters are put together in some other way

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol: dry

explanation.surface: Groundsmen somehow keeping a cricket pitch dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the four letters as MAED before 'to keep' wraps them round. In cricket a wicket is the pitch, and some pitches are laid with coconut matting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket pitch covered with coconut matting is a matting wicket, one kind of pitch.

clue.text: Our community record that is sure initially to get plaudits

parts.note: EU, the European Union, was once the European Community
a log is a record
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A European body's archive is sure to win praise from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeches of high praise are tributes, so plaudits is a near synonym.

clue.text: No street for joker — bad reception

indicators.note: No says the street's letters are not there

parts.note: a jester is a court joker

explanation.surface: A comedian gets a poor reception because he isn't on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No street' removes ST from JESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mocking shout from an audience is a hostile welcome, a noun sense.

clue.text: Hot rod awry — needing repair to make it this?

definitions.text: Hot rod awry — needing repair to make it this?

indicators.note: something needing repair has to be put back together, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A souped-up car has gone wrong and must be fixed before it is fit to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing repair' rearranges HOT ROD AWRY; the whole clue is also the definition, since a fixed car is fit for the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A car in a safe state for use on public highways is fit to drive.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed about wayward teenager — must be radically changed

indicators.note: about means the red goes round the other letters

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red

indicators.note: wayward says the letters of the word stray from their order

explanation.surface: A blushing parent says an unruly teenager needs to change completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' turns TEENAGER into GENERATE, and RED goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something renewed or reformed thoroughly has been transformed, a synonym.

clue.text: I phone inside old college, speaking respectfully?

indicators.note: inside says the I and phone go within the college

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a type of UK college now gone
TEL is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: A student making a call from a former college, and being courteous about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Polytechnics were UK colleges that became universities in 1992, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking courteously is talking in a well-mannered way; the adverb describes how one speaks.

clue.text: After struggle, hoper wins possession

indicators.note: after a struggle things are knocked about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A hopeful player fights and finally gains the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After struggle' looks like a time phrase in a sporting story, but it is the signal to rearrange the nine letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Possession of something means having legal title to it: a synonym.

clue.text: Barbecue bun without hesitation rejected as food

indicators.note: rejected means the remaining letters are sent back, read in reverse
without says the hesitation is taken out

parts.note: a burger is a bun cooked on a barbecue
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A barbecue burger is turned down without a moment's pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes ER from BURGER, leaving BURG; 'rejected' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal slang for something to eat.

clue.text: Stand still as guy at party has fallen finally at end of dance

parts.note: a stag is the man at a stag party

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of fallen
end of picks the closing letter of the word dance that follows

explanation.surface: A groom-to-be collapses at the end of the dance and stands motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is the British send-off for a man about to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain inactive and not develop is to stagnate, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Writer about two cultures — the stuff of a cold man

definitions.meaning: C. P. ... wrote the 1959 lecture The Two Cultures on the arts and sciences

definitions.text: the stuff of a cold man
definitions.meaning: a cold man is one built in winter, made of white flakes

explanation.surface: A novelist on the arts and sciences is called the material of a frosty person.
explanation.walkthrough: The cold man is the figure built in a garden in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: C. P. Snow, the English novelist-scientist, and the white flakes from which a winter figure is built.

clue.text: A time with careful listener

parts.note: tender in the sense of gentle, careful in handling

explanation.surface: Someone who has been careful at one time is a good listener.
explanation.definitionFit: One who pays attention, as to a speaker, is heeding them; an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Cleric gets to eat around six

indicators.note: around says the eating word goes round the six

parts.note: to dine is to eat
VI is the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: A vicar gets to have supper at about six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reads as 'approximately', as in about six o'clock, but it is the container signal; 'gets' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A divine is an old word for a clergyman or theologian, a noun sense.

clue.text: Not parasitic like the hippies?

definitions.meaning: in biology an organism living independently, not on a host
hippies were known for a carefree, unconventional lifestyle

explanation.surface: Hippies are praised as not sponging off anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A biology term for organisms that live independently, and a phrase for an unconstrained lifestyle.

clue.text: What's charged when there's penny off grocery item

indicators.note: off means the penny is removed

parts.note: the price is what is charged

explanation.surface: A shop knocks a penny off the cost of something on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes the P from PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple grain bought from a grocer is an example of a shop item.

clue.text: Plant that might be revealed by American naturalist

indicators.note: revealed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A flower that an American botanist might discover.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'Plant'; 'that might be' is a link joining it to the indicator 'revealed by', not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical genus with bright flowers and large leaves, grown as an ornamental: an example of a flowering species.

clue.text: Soon quiet instrument is to be introduced

indicators.note: the instrument and is are brought into the call for quiet

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
a harp is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A quiet instrument will be brought in shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpish is British informal for quickly, without delay.

clue.text: After conclusion of dinner I love port

indicators.note: conclusion of picks the last letter of dinner

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: After the meal finishes, someone confesses a fondness for port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the after-dinner drink; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian harbour city, an example of a seaport.

clue.text: The stage is temporary

definitions.meaning: the stage means the theatrical profession, performing
as in an interim manager, filling a role for the time being

explanation.surface: A claim that the theatre is only a passing thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing in plays is the stage profession, and an interim chairman holds the post temporarily.

clue.text: Resist work when facing endless problem

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: endless says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: Someone holds out when confronted with a never-ending task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the R off POSER.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist a plan is to stand against it: a synonym.

clue.text: Process to pursue drug in sport

indicators.note: to pursue means to follow, so this piece comes after the drug

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
a way of doing something is a process or method

explanation.surface: An inquiry chasing a drug cheat in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: SPEEDWAY is motorcycle racing on oval dirt tracks, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorcycle racing on short oval tracks is a spectator sport of that name.
